newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SKF sees unchanged economic picture 1997.
newsitem.headline: SKF sees unchanged economic picture 1997.

text.p: Swedish ballbearing company SKF AB's president Peter Augustsson said on Friday he expects the business cycle to be unchanged in the next six months, meaning flat production levels for the company.
"Overall we expect the business cycle picture to be unchanged from our point of view, at least for the coming half year. This means we will see even volumes," Augustsson told Reuters in an interview.
He said the downturn in the European business cycle has stopped but signs of an upturn were difficult to detect.
"The differences between various European countries are large. Spain and England are strong, Germany is fairly okay while Italy is weak. There are, however, no dramatic changes," he said.
"In the U.S. development continues to be positive and even if the upturn in the economy tapers off, 1997 will still be a good year," Augustsson said.
"Growth in Eastern Europe is strong and there we are growing more than the total market. The same is true in central Europe," he said.
There is still a high rate of growth in Asia as well as for SKF sales in the region. Korea and Japan are exceptions -- here the economy has weakened.
"So our forecast in the nine month report last autumn, that the business climate will be largely unchanged for the next few quarters, is still valid," he said.
